how.title: How it works
how.step1Body: Country, year, and how many leave days you can take. That's it.
how.step2Body: We look for the short gap where one leave day connects a holiday to the weekend.
how.step3Body: The highlight is the stretch with the most days off. Breaks that are already free sit in their own list.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: How do a holiday and a weekend join?
faq.a1: A long break you get when a public holiday lands near the weekend and you use one or more leave days to connect them.
faq.q2: Does a Saturday or Sunday holiday add an extra day?
faq.a2: No. If it already falls on the weekend, it doesn't add a weekday off. It can still sit inside a longer break.
faq.q3: How do you pick the best option?
faq.a3: The highlighted break is the longest one. If two last the same, the one that uses fewer vacation days comes first.
faq.a4: The full calendar today is Chile, for 2027. Argentina, Mexico, Spain, Brazil, Peru, and Colombia show up as coming soon.
faq.a5: Not yet. Only national holidays count. A regional holiday can lengthen the break where you live, but it isn't in this calculation.
faq.q6: Do you store what I calculate?
faq.a6: No. The math runs in your browser. We don't ask for an account or send your vacation days to a server.

about.p1: MoreDays helps you stretch the vacation you already have, using the public holidays on the calendar.
about.p2: You pick a country, a year, and how many leave days you can take. You get concrete dates: how many days off you gain and how many vacation days you spend.
about.p3: The detail today is Chile. The other countries in the selector will arrive once the calendar is confirmed.

privacy.p1: MoreDays has no accounts and doesn't store what you calculate.
privacy.p2: The combination is built in your browser. Your vacation days are not sent to a server of ours.
privacy.p3: If we turn on ads, the slot will be labeled and the provider may use its own cookies. Until then, we don't load ads.
privacy.p4: TODO: add the site owner and a contact email before launch.

terms.p1: MoreDays is a guide for planning time off. It is not employment or legal advice.
terms.p2: Dates come from public sources. Confirm them before you request leave: a new law can move a holiday.
terms.p3: The service is provided as is. We don't promise your employer will approve a combination.
